bottleneck.description: On-orbit servicing and active debris-removal operator (ADRAS-J, ELSA, life extension); holds flown rendezvous-and-proximity-operations heritage but no concentrated supply-chain position.

dependency.key_customers: JAXA, US Space Force, ESA / UK Space Agency, Eutelsat (life extension)

editorial.notes: Astroscale has genuine first-mover flight heritage: ADRAS-J is the first spacecraft to safely approach and characterise a large piece of orbital debris. That is a capability lead, not a control point. On-orbit servicing is an emerging, contestable service and the anchor customers deliberately multi-source it; the US Space Force ran its Tetra refuelling demonstrations across Astroscale, Northrop Grumman and Orbit Fab, and Northrop's life-extension vehicle is already operational. It fails the concentration and in-volume-dependence tests, so it rates LOW, the strongest of a weak-choke set. Revenue is demonstration and government-anchored rather than recurring.
